decisions.executionNote: Begin continuous elbow-up approach to the inner white supports on each side; orient grippers downward-forward while keeping open.
Align open jaws with the angled inner supports, lowering gradually; right support is farther back than left.
Use wrist views to center each support between the jaws, advancing and lowering in small increments before closing.
Fine-align the white supports, close both grippers, then make a short vertical retention-test lift.
Both supports appear retained. Lift clear and begin moving them toward symmetric base positions, gradually straightening their yaw.
Center the two retained supports at symmetric base locations and finish aligning them upright; descend partway without releasing.
Set both upright supports gently onto the table at matching depth, open the jaws, and begin a short clearance lift.
Clear the released supports, then move outward and slowly turn both open grippers toward the ends of the long lower board.
Finish orienting the grippers inward above opposite ends of the long board; supports appear upright and separated symmetrically.
Approach the long board from both ends with matched inward/downward motion and open jaws, correcting small wrist orientation residuals.
Close both jaws around the long board and lift its ends together a short distance to verify retention and levelness.
Lift the long board further clear of the table, keeping both ends level, then translate toward the two upright base supports.
Align the board depth over the two supports, then lower both ends equally to near their top faces, retaining the board for visual confirmation.
Gently seat the lower board across both supports, open both grippers, then withdraw outward and upward to check stability.
Lower board remains on both supports. Reorient open grippers and move separately toward the two remaining white blocks for the middle supports.
Approach the remaining white blocks from above, adjusting yaw to their visible orientations; keep open and use the next wrist views for fine centering.
Correct the left block's lateral offset and advance the right wrist toward its farther-back block, lowering both open grippers in small increments.
Grasp and test-lift the centered left support. The right block remains off-center; back upward and remove wrist yaw before a new visual alignment.
Lift and carry the retained left block inward. Reapproach the rotated right block from higher clearance, compensating wrist position while matching its long-axis yaw.
Carry the left support above its middle-layer position. Lower the now-aligned right gripper toward its block, with small lateral and yaw corrections.
Seat and release the left middle support on the lower board. Fine-center and close on the right support, followed by a short retention-test lift.
Right support appears retained. Lift it clear and start transferring inward while straightening yaw; withdraw the open left hand from the placed support.
Transfer the right support above the lower board without descending yet. Position the open left hand above the left end of the middle board.
Lower the right support toward the matching middle-layer location while aligning the open left gripper at the middle board's left end.
Seat and release the right middle support, then lift the open hand away without disturbing the lower board. Keep the left hand poised at the middle board.
Move the open right hand away from the stable middle support toward the middle board's right end, gradually turning inward with configuration continuity.
Finish aligning the right gripper inward and descend toward the middle board, matching the waiting left hand's grasp height.
Resolve the right wrist's contact/tracking offset with a small outward clearance and slower alignment at the board end before grasping.
Close both grippers on the middle board and lift the ends together for a short retention check.
Raise the retained middle board above the middle-support tops, preserving a level two-handed grasp before translating toward the tower.
Translate the level middle board above the two middle supports, keeping its height fixed and both grippers closed.
Lower the centered middle board evenly onto the two supports, retaining both ends while checking contact and alignment.
Release the seated middle board, then withdraw both open grippers outward and upward to verify it remains centered and stable.
The middle layer remains stable. Move separately toward the green cap on the left and small wooden top board on the right, keeping open and above the pieces.
Continue the separate top-piece approaches slowly, bringing the green cap and small board into the wrist views before final descent.
Lower toward the green cap while shifting and straightening the right gripper to center the small wooden board in its wrist view.
Make final wrist-based centering corrections, close around both top pieces, and lift briefly to verify retention before transfer.
Both top pieces appear retained. Lift above the tower and begin turning the small board to align with the middle layer; keep the green cap safely to the left.
Carry the small top board inward above the tower and finish its yaw alignment. Hold the green cap at a separate left-side staging position.
Center the small wooden board above the completed middle layer, then begin a gentle vertical descent; keep the green cap clear on the left.
Fine-center and seat the small top board, open the right gripper, then withdraw upward and right while holding the green cap clear.
Correct the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Carry the cap above the top board while withdrawing the open right arm gradually toward home.
Fine-center and lower the green cap toward the small top board; continue the right arm's gradual open-gripper return toward origin.
Seat and release the centered green cap, withdraw leftward and upward, and finish the right arm's slow open-gripper return to origin.
The cap remains upright on the top board. Withdraw the open left arm backward with ample height and smoothly turn toward its home orientation; hold the right near origin.
Return the open left arm smoothly to its origin while leaving the completed tower untouched and the right arm at home.
